questions.question:
**Direction:** Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. On the answer sheet, darken the circle of the correct answer against each question.

B. You must select the best answer for each question.

C. Every question is followed by four answer choices marked 1, 2, 3 and 4.

D. If you darken more than one circle, the answer will be counted as wrong.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CBAD'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• *By reading the given lines, we can interpret that the speaker is talking about the answer sheet and the questions which are given in the examination.*
 
• *The opening sentence will be C- In this sentence, the speaker explains that the question has four options and it is marked with the numeric value.*
 
• *The next sentence will be B- In this sentence, the speaker explains that we need to select the options by marking the numeric value.*
 
• *The next sentence will be A- In this sentence, the speaker explains that we need to encircle the correct answer again the question number.*
 
• *The next sentence will be D- In this sentence, the speaker explains how the incorrect question is counted.*

**Hence, the correct sequence is-** **CBAD i.e. Option 3.**

questions.question:
Direction: **The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Please give me / a kilo of potatoes, / two kilos of tomatoes and / a bunch coriander leaves.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'a bunch coriander leaves'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** error lies in** the part **'a bunch coriander leaves'.**
 
• The *preposition* **'of' **must be used before** 'coriander leaves'.**
 
• The *preposition ***'of'** is used used ***after words or phrases expressing amount, number, or a particular unit***, as in this case,** 'a bunch'.**
 
 
• **Example:**__
 
 
• *A kilo** of **apples.*
 
• *Hundreds **of** people.*
 
• *A drop **of** rain.*
 
• *A speck **of** dust.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the *preposition* **'of'** must be used to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 1.**

**Correct sentence:** *Please give me a kilo of potatoes, two kilos of tomatoes and a bunch of coriander leaves.*
